what: A screen-height stage is pinned (sticky) inside a long panel and draws a flock of posters (three instanced mesh, up to 64). As you scroll they pass through the plan’s formations in order: fly (scattered inside a 30×17×32 box, drifting toward the camera), wall (8-column wall tilted back −.95rad and turned −.5rad), ring (donut of radius 3.4 and 3.9, facing outward like petals), grid (6×6), roll (three rows on a radius 3.2 cylinder), field (scattered field), stack (pile of 12), trail (diagonal trail of 14), carousel (single row), gone (drops out below). Each formation moves during its last 40%, and the scroll value follows through a spring (natural frequency 18, critically damped) so it stops slightly late after you let go. Fast-moving posters split and smear in RGB

options.plan: Names of large items to fly past (comma-separated), default fly,wall,ring,grid,roll,field,stack,trail
options.count: Number of posters (max 64), default the larger of the item count and 48
options.side: Horizontal offset (world units, right is +) for moving rings, checkerboards, etc., default 0
options.[data-fx-part=stage]: Screen-height stage (child) — if none, draw on the element itself
options.[data-fx-part=item]: Poster (child, hidden) — if it has an img use that photo, data-title and text are placeholder lettering
